key_insight: EventNeuS is the first self-supervised method that combines 3D signed-distance implicit geometry with monocular colour event streams to produce dense 3D mesh reconstructions from a single event camera, improving reconstruction accuracy from event data.
problem_solved: Existing event-based approaches struggle to produce accurate, dense 3D meshes from monocular event-camera input; EventNeuS addresses the gap by enabling high-quality 3D surface reconstruction directly from event streams without ground-truth meshes.
method: Encode monocular colour event streams into a continuous representation and feed them to a neural implicit surface model based on a 3D signed-distance function (SDF).
Self-supervise training with event-driven consistency cues and colour information (no ground-truth meshes required), jointly optimizing geometry and appearance.
Extract a dense triangle mesh from the learned SDF for downstream use (visualization, metric evaluation, or further processing).
impact: Provides practitioners a practical route to dense, accurate 3D reconstruction in scenarios where event cameras excel (high speed, high dynamic range, low latency), enabling robust 3D perception pipelines that do not rely on multi-view RGB or ground-truth meshes.
